note: Terrain tuning (docs/08). Albedos are linear and physical; the painted look comes from the palette at tonemap (docs/05).

islands.note: Islands to start from (recipes/land/<id>.json). `?island=<id>` picks one; without it the starter island. The badge in the top left corner switches between them (each starts fresh until saves arrive in S7).

detail.note: Scanned ground detail (docs/22). Layers follow the material weight order: grass, sand, rock, soil. Colors still come from materials.albedo*; the scans add variation around them.

hex.note: Hex tiling (G2, high and medium tiers). density: triangle-grid vertices per tile along one axis (Mikkelsen uses 2 * sqrt(3); 2 keeps whole stones). sharpness: weight exponent before the height bias; higher means narrower seams.

twoScale.note: Low tier: a second read at size x the tile, mixed in by noise of noiseMeters.

macro.note: Slow tone drift on all tiers. scalesM: the two noise sizes; strength: brightness swing; second: weight of the smaller one; hue: warm-cool swing.

grain.note: Drifting grain (G4, hex tiling tiers): each hex vertex turns its copy of the scan by a slow angle field (up to spreadDeg either way, varying over fieldM meters) plus jitterDeg of random turn, and scales it by up to scaleJitter, so a large patch has no common direction. layers: how much of it each scan takes (0 none, 1 all); cliff takes a little so cliff faces stay mostly upright.

cliff.note: Rock's scan on steep faces (G4): the rock layer reads it in place of its flat scan past steepDeg. Wet look uses rock's porosity.

moss.note: Live moss (interim until doc 10's growth system): grows where the water summary says the ground stays damp (hollows of at least minHollowM2, banks of ponds and streams, never the tide band). growHours: game hours for a cell to fill once reached; it spreads to a neighbor once cover passes spreadFrom; fadeHours: game hours to vanish where the ground dried out.
moss.maxCoverNote: The most moss each ground can carry, even fully grown: grass competes and always shows through; damp soil and stone hold the most; loose sand (painted, or the beach band) dries fast and shifts. In the terrain shader moss is a soft, clumpy partial cover below this cap, and the height blend lets grass tufts and stone tops stand through it.

wetness.note: Visual wetness (docs/08; world/terrain/wetness.js, terrain-wetness.wgsl). Rebuilt every intervalS real seconds (lowTierIntervalS on the low tier). Held at 1 under live water deeper than waterDepthM (from the first to the second depth) and below the tide, plus a splash band tideBandM above it; damp hollows hold water.json look.dampHollowWet. Rain soaks it at rainSoakPerHour x intensity per game hour. Spreads bankSpreadM into banks (linear fade; each meter of climb counts as bankRiseWeight meters). Where nothing holds it, it falls from soaked to dry in dryHours game hours, times sunFactor (night, then full sun at sunFullDeg and above) and 1 + windFactor x wind; no drying while rain passes rainStopsDrying. Look: wetness above sheenFrom moves ground roughness toward wetRoughness, by up to wetRoughnessShare.

wetGround.note: G3 wet ground (docs/22, after Lagarde 2013), driven by the visual wetness map (wetness above). damp: soaked ground's roughness and albedo factor for dense ground (rock) and porous ground (soil, sand), blended by each material's detail.layers porosity; so sand and soil go dark and satin, rock darkens a little and turns shiny. Wet ground and puddles reflect the sky probe; dry ground stays matte. puddles: on ground flatter than flatDeg (full below the first angle, none past the second), rain raises a level at fillPerHour at full rain; it drains over drainHours of drying (sun and wind speed it, as for wetness). Water stands where the ground's relief is below the level: the detail height (ruts, the gaps between stones) mixed with a slow undulation of undulationM by undulationShare, so puddles gather in real dips first; maxCover is the most of the low spots a full level covers; turf: on grass the level rises this much less (turf soaks rain up), so only the deepest meadow dips flood. Puddle water: roughness, albedo factor of the bed under it, f0 of water. Raindrop rings in puddles use water.json ripples.rings.

underwater.note: The ground under live water (ponds, streams, the sea). bedDepthM: water depths over which grass gives way to a bare soil bed (sand and stone stay), so the waterline reads from straight above. siltDepthM: depths over which fine mud (materials.albedoSilt) settles on the soft bed; siltCover: the most of the bed it covers.

drownedMeadow.note: Under shallow, still water a grassy bed keeps its drowned grass, weed and algae (a marsh floor, a pond's shallow margin), so from above it reads olive rather than bare silt, right from the waterline. albedo: linear, physical (submerged plants; the wet look then darkens it like any soaked ground); cover: the most of the bed it covers, in mottled patches; depthM: water depths over which it gives way to bare silt; stillMps: water speeds over which running water scours it away.
